mainTopic: Life needed at the end of a process and signs of life in שחיטה; whether a נכרי owner's thoughts can disqualify a Jew's שחיטה
overview: The עמוד opens by finishing a ברייתא that reads each phrase of the פסוק about קרבנות as excluding a kind of animal. The last phrase, 'תחת אמו', excludes a יתום. The גמרא shows that this יתום must be an animal whose mother died at the very end of its birth. From that it proves that when life is required, it must last to the end of the process, and this is why a בהמה מסוכנת must show life at the end of שחיטה. רבא then rules like a ברייתא: a small animal that stretched out its foreleg and did not pull it back is פסולה. Every other leg movement counts as a sign of life, and so does even a small flutter of a bird's wing or wag of its tail. The bird rule is the new point, since our משנה does not mention birds. A new משנה follows: a Jew who slaughters for a נכרי. The תנא קמא says the שחיטה is valid, רבי אליעזר disqualifies it, and רבי יוסי argues with a קל וחומר that only the שוחט's thoughts count. The גמרא gives two explanations of the dispute, and the second one continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: The ברייתא finishes reading the פסוק about which animals can be קרבנות
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues reading each phrase of the פסוק as excluding a certain kind of animal from being a קרבן. The last phrase, 'תחת אמו', excludes a יתום.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Or a sheep' excludes כלאים. 'Or a goat' excludes a נדמה. 'When it is born' excludes a יוצא דופן. 'Seven days' excludes a מחוסר זמן. 'Under its mother' excludes a יתום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting the rest of a ברייתא that lists animals that cannot be brought as a קרבן, one for each phrase of the פסוק. The last item, the יתום, is the one the גמרא will use for its proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each phrase of the פסוק adds a condition the animal must meet. Most of the list is simple, but 'תחת אמו' excluding a יתום raises a question: what kind of orphan is meant? The next steps work that out, and the answer will prove something about needing life at the end of a process.

keyTerms.meaning: to exclude; this phrase of the פסוק leaves out the following case
an animal born from two different species
an animal that looks like a different species than its parents
an animal born by cutting open the mother's side, not through a normal birth
an animal that is not yet old enough (under eight days)
an orphan; here, a newborn animal whose mother died

phrases.english: "Or a sheep" — to exclude an animal of mixed species,
phrases.notes: The ברייתא is reading ויקרא 22:27 phrase by phrase, and its beginning came just before this part.

phrases.english: "Or a goat" — to exclude one that looks like another species,
"When it is born" — to exclude one born through the side,
"Seven days" — to exclude one not yet old enough,
"Under its mother" — to exclude an orphan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא the גמרא began quoting just before this part, as a source for whether life is needed at the end of a process.
steps.raayaObject: Whether life is required at the end of a process (such as שחיטה or birth).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא reading ויקרא 22:27, especially 'תחת אמו' excluding a יתום.

steps.title: What kind of orphan? Not one whose mother died after a normal birth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly a יתום is here. It rejects the idea that the mother died some time after the birth, since every mother dies eventually.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this orphan? If you say its mother gave birth to it and then died, should the mother live forever?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what case of יתום the ברייתא means and knocks down the first possible answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'orphan' just meant the mother died some time after the birth, almost every animal would end up disqualified, because mothers don't live forever. That can't be what the פסוק means, so the גמרא has to look for a different case.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the case? how does it look?
if you say; introduces a suggested answer that will be tested
keep on living (literally, live and go on)

phrases.english: This orphan, what is the case?
If you say its mother gave birth to it and then died,
should she live on forever?
phrases.notes: He means every mother dies eventually, so this can't be the orphan the פסוק means.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the exact case of the יתום mentioned at the end of the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What case of 'orphan' does 'תחת אמו' exclude?

steps.title: Not one whose mother died before the birth either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the mother died first and then the baby came out, but rejects it because that case is already covered by 'כי יולד'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the mother died and then gave birth to it? That is already learned from 'when it is born.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second meaning of 'orphan' and rejects it as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the mother is already dead, the baby can't come out through a normal birth, so it is like a יוצא דופן. That was already excluded by 'כי יולד' in step 1, so 'תחת אמו' would add nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: and afterward; and then
it comes out; it is already learned from (another phrase)

phrases.english: Rather, where she died and then gave birth to it,
that is already learned from "when it is born."
phrases.notes: This points back to step 1, where 'כי יולד' excluded a יוצא דופן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second possible case after step 2 rejected the first, and rejects it too.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading 'יתום' as an animal whose mother died before the birth.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That case is already excluded by 'כי יולד', so 'תחת אמו' would add nothing.

steps.title: The orphan is one whose mother died right at the end of the birth
steps.stepSummary: Since both other options failed, the גמרא concludes the case must be where, at the very end of the birth, the mother died just as the baby came out alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obvious: this one left for death and that one left for life.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the only case of יתום that is left: the mother dies at the exact moment the birth finishes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mother was alive when the birth started but dead at the moment the baby fully came out. So the question becomes: does it matter that she was not alive at the END of the birth? The next step uses this.

keyTerms.meaning: it is obvious
separated, left (here: one left toward death, the other toward life)

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious:

phrases.aramaic: זֶה פֵּירַשׁ לְמִיתָה וְזֶה פֵּירַשׁ לְחַיִּים.
phrases.english: this one left for death, and that one left for life.
phrases.notes: The mother died at the very moment the baby came out alive.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא פְּשִׁיטָא, זֶה פֵּירַשׁ לְמִיתָה וְזֶה פֵּירַשׁ לְחַיִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2 after both suggestions were rejected.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The יתום is an animal whose mother died right at the end of its birth.

steps.title: So life is needed at the end of the process
steps.stepSummary: A separate פסוק to exclude this orphan only makes sense if the mother must be alive at the end of the birth. If not, the case would already be covered by 'כי יולד'. So life is required at the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say we need life at the end of the birth, that is why a פסוק was needed to exclude it. But if you say we do not need life at the end of the birth, why do I need it? It is already learned from 'when it is born.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws its proof: the ברייתא only makes sense if life is required at the end of the birth, so life is required at the end of a process.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If being alive at the start were enough, this mother counts as alive and there is nothing to exclude. Then the only orphan left is one whose mother died before the birth, already covered by 'כי יולד', and 'תחת אמו' would be extra. Since the תורה bothered to write it, being alive at the end must matter. The same idea applies to the end of שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: it makes sense if...; this works if...
life at the end (of the process)
a פסוק was needed
to exclude

steps.whatToRemember: The orphan of 'תחת אמו' is a mother that died right at the end of the birth. A פסוק is only needed for this if life at the end of the process matters, so we learn that life is required at the end.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the rule that a בהמה מסוכנת must show a sign of life at the end of its שחיטה, not only at the beginning.

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא בָּעֵינַן חִיּוּתָא בְּסוֹף לֵידָה –
phrases.english: It makes sense if you say we require life at the end of the birth —
that is why a verse was needed to exclude it,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ לָא בָּעֵינַן חִיּוּתָא בְּסוֹף לֵידָה,
phrases.english: but if you say we do not require life at the end of the birth,
why is it needed? It is already learned from "when it is born"!
phrases.notes: Without this rule, the only orphan left would be the one from step 3, already covered by 'כי יולד'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא בָּעֵינַן חִיּוּתָא בְּסוֹף לֵידָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the case set up in step 4 to prove that life is required at the end of a process.
steps.raayaObject: Life is required at the end of a process.
steps.raayaSupportSource: 'תחת אמו' would add nothing beyond 'כי יולד' unless life at the end of the birth is required.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: We require life at the end of the process.

steps.title: רבא rules on a small animal that stretched out its foreleg
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that the הלכה follows a ברייתא: a small animal that stretched out its foreleg during שחיטה and did not pull it back is פסולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The הלכה is like this ברייתא: a small animal that stretched out its foreleg and did not bring it back is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a detail from the משנה about signs of life, and רבא rules that the הלכה follows a ברייתא on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a small animal, just stretching out the foreleg without pulling it back does not count as a sign of life. So the שחיטה is פסולה. This fits the idea that a real sign of life is needed at the end of the process.

keyTerms.meaning: the הלכה follows...
a teaching of the תנאים; here, a ברייתא
a small animal, like a sheep or goat
stretched out its foreleg
invalid; the שחיטה does not count

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: הִלְכְתָא כִּי הָא מַתְנִיתָא –
phrases.english: Rava said: The halakha follows this baraita —

phrases.aramaic: בְּהֵמָה דַּקָּה שֶׁפָּשְׁטָה יָדָהּ וְלֹא הֶחְזִירָה, פְּסוּלָה.
phrases.english: a small animal that stretched out its foreleg and did not bring it back is invalid.
phrases.notes: This is about a very sick animal being slaughtered, where we look for a sign that it was still alive.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הִלְכְתָא כִּי הָא מַתְנִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After proving life is needed at the end, the גמרא turns to a practical ruling about which movements count as a sign of life.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A small animal that stretched out its foreleg during שחיטה and did not pull it back is פסולה.

steps.title: The rest of the ברייתא: foreleg, small animals, and birds
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא limits the 'stretched foreleg = not alive' rule to the foreleg of a small animal. Any leg movement of a large animal, and even a tiny flutter of a bird, counts as a sign of life.
steps.simpleTranslation: When is this said? Only about the foreleg. But with the hind leg, whether it stretched out and did not bend back, or bent and did not stretch out, the שחיטה is valid. When is this said? Only about a small animal. But with a large animal, whether the foreleg or the hind leg, and whether it stretched and did not bend back or bent and did not stretch, it is valid. And a bird, even if it only fluttered its wing or only wagged its tail, that counts as a sign of life.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the ברייתא from the previous step and shows how narrow its 'פסולה' rule is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only one case is a bad sign: a small animal stretching its foreleg without pulling it back, which is just the body dying. Every other movement, a hind leg or any leg of a large animal, shows real life. For a bird, even the smallest movement of the wing or tail counts.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case is this said? (a phrase that limits a rule)
Small animal (sheep, goat) / large animal (cattle)
Stretched out / bent in
A movement or jerk that shows the animal was still alive at שחיטה
Fluttered (a wing) / wagged (a tail)

steps.confusionAlert: 'כשרה' here means the שחיטה is valid because the movement proves the animal was alive. It does not mean the movement itself is needed in every case.

phrases.english: In what case is this said? With the foreleg,
but with the hind leg,
whether it stretched it out and did not bend it back,
or bent it and did not stretch it out, it is valid.
In what case is this said? With a small animal,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּגַסָּה, בֵּין בַּיָּד בֵּין בָּרֶגֶל,
phrases.english: but with a large animal, whether the foreleg or the hind leg,
whether it stretched it out and did not bend it back,
or bent it and did not stretch it out, it is valid.

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹף, אֲפִילּוּ לֹא רִפְרֵף אֶלָּא גַּפּוֹ,
phrases.english: And a bird, even if it only fluttered its wing,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא כִּשְׁכֵּשׁ אֶלָּא זְנָבוֹ – הֲרֵי זֶה פִּירְכּוּס.
phrases.english: or only wagged its tail, that is a sign of life.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא that רבא ruled like in Step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a small animal's stretched foreleg is not a sign of life. Any leg of a large animal, a hind leg, or even a bird's wing or tail movement is a sign of life.

steps.title: What did רבא add? The משנה already says this
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבא had to rule like the ברייתא, since our משנה already teaches the foreleg rule and its limits.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us? We already learned all of it! 'A small animal that stretched its foreleg and did not pull it back is פסולה, because that is only the soul leaving.' A foreleg, yes; a hind leg, no. A small animal, yes; a large animal, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא: his ruling seems to add nothing, because the משנה already says it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה names only 'a small animal' and 'its foreleg.' From that wording we can already tell that a hind leg or a large animal is different. So the ברייתא's limits seem to be already built into the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us? (asked when a statement seems to add nothing new)
We already learned all of them
The soul leaving the body; the normal motion of dying, not a sign of life
Yes / no (used here to show what we learn from the משנה's wording)

phrases.aramaic: מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן? כּוּלְּהוּ תְּנַנְהִי!
phrases.english: What is he teaching us? We already learned all of them!

phrases.aramaic: בְּהֵמָה דַּקָּה שֶׁפָּשְׁטָה יָדָהּ וְלֹא הֶחְזִירָה – פְּסוּלָה,
phrases.english: A small animal that stretched out its foreleg and did not pull it back is not valid,
since it is only the soul leaving.
A foreleg, yes; a hind leg, no.
A small animal, yes; a large animal, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן? כּוּלְּהוּ תְּנַנְהִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for רבא's ruling on the ברייתא quoted in Steps 6-7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that the הלכה follows the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's wording already implies everything the ברייתא says about legs and animal size, so the ruling seems to add nothing.

steps.title: The new part is the bird
steps.stepSummary: רבא needed to rule like the ברייתא because of the bird rule, which the משנה does not mention.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needed it for the bird, which we did not learn in the משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question: the bird rule is what רבא is really teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animal rules are already in the משנה, but birds are not mentioned there at all. The ברייתא's teaching that even a wing flutter or tail wag counts as life is new information, so רבא's ruling is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed for him (to teach this)
Which we did not learn (in the משנה)

steps.whatToRemember: רבא rules like the ברייתא mainly for the bird: even a small flutter of the wing or wag of the tail shows it was alive.

phrases.english: He needed it for a bird, which we did not learn.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a new point that the earlier source did not teach
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא's ruling seemed to repeat what the משנה already teaches.
steps.terutzMaskana: His ruling is needed for the bird case, which is missing from the משנה.

steps.title: New משנה: slaughtering for a נכרי
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that a Jew's שחיטה for a נכרי is valid. רבי אליעזר disqualifies it, because we assume the נכרי means it for עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A Jew who slaughters for a נכרי: his שחיטה is valid, and רבי אליעזר disqualifies it. רבי אליעזר said: Even if he slaughtered it to feed the נכרי from its diaphragm, it is not valid, because a נכרי's usual intention is for עבודה זרה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a מחלוקת about whether a נכרי's intention can ruin a Jew's שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling of the משנה is that the שחיטה is valid. רבי אליעזר says the נכרי's assumed thoughts of עבודה זרה count, even if the נכרי will only eat a small, unimportant part of the animal.

keyTerms.meaning: One who slaughters for a non-Jew
Disqualifies
The diaphragm (a small, unimportant part near the liver)
A non-Jew's usual, unstated intention
Idol worship

steps.confusionAlert: The one doing the שחיטה is a Jew. The question is only whether the נכרי owner's assumed thoughts can make it פסולה.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who slaughters for a non-Jew, his slaughter is valid,
and Rabbi Eliezer disqualifies it.
Rabbi Eliezer said: Even if he slaughtered it

phrases.aramaic: לֶאֱכוֹל לְנׇכְרִי מֵחֲצַר כָּבֵד שֶׁלָּהּ – פְּסוּלָה,
phrases.english: to feed the non-Jew from its diaphragm, it is not valid,
phrases.notes: Even this small, unimportant part is enough, in רבי אליעזר's view.

phrases.english: because a non-Jew's usual intention is for idol worship.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Jew's שחיטה for a נכרי is valid. רבי אליעזר disqualifies it because of the נכרי's assumed thoughts of עבודה זרה.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's קל וחומר: only the slaughterer's thoughts count
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי argues: with קדשים, where thoughts can ruin the שחיטה, only the one doing the עבודה counts. So with חולין, where thoughts are less powerful, surely only the שוחט counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: This is a קל וחומר. With קדשים, where thoughts can disqualify, everything follows only the one doing the service. With חולין, where thoughts do not disqualify, isn't it logical that everything follows only the slaughterer?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי argues against רבי אליעזר with a קל וחומר, to prove the owner's thoughts do not matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In קדשים a wrong thought really can ruin a קרבן, yet only the כהן doing the service's thoughts count, not the owner's. חולין is a weaker case for thoughts, so the owner's (the נכרי's) thoughts surely do not count there either, only the Jewish שוחט's.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a stronger case to a weaker one
A thought that disqualifies
Holy animals set aside as קרבנות
Ordinary, non-holy animals
The one doing the service (the כהן)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי: what counts is the intention of the person doing the act (the שוחט), not the owner.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: קַל וָחוֹמֶר הַדְּבָרִים,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said: The matter is an a fortiori argument,
if in a place where thought disqualifies, with holy animals,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין הַכֹּל הוֹלֵךְ אֶלָּא אַחַר הָעוֹבֵד,
phrases.english: everything follows only the one doing the service,
phrases.notes: He means the כהן's thoughts count, not the owner's who brought the קרבן.

phrases.english: then in a place where thought does not disqualify, with ordinary animals,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא הַכֹּל הוֹלֵךְ
phrases.english: isn't it logical that everything should follow
only the slaughterer?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: קַל וָחוֹמֶר הַדְּבָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues against רבי אליעזר's view in Step 10.
steps.raayaObject: That a נכרי owner's thoughts do not disqualify a Jew's שחיטה; only the שוחט's thoughts count
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from קדשים, where only the thoughts of the one doing the service count

steps.title: The shared basis: owners can ruin a קרבן with their thoughts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the תנאים of the משנה follow רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי, who holds that the owners, not only the כהן, can make a קרבן פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: These תנאים hold like רבי אליעזר son of רבי יוסי. It was taught that he said: I heard that the owners can make a קרבן פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the משנה. It says the two sides of the משנה share one basic idea: the owner's thoughts can ruin a שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only the שוחט's thoughts counted, a נכרי owner's thoughts could never matter. By tying the משנה to רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי, the גמרא explains why the owner's thought of עבודה זרה is even a question. This sets up the next step, which explains what the תנאים do argue about.

keyTerms.meaning: make a קרבן פיגול (ruined by a wrong thought)
the owners of the animal
the תנאים, the sages of the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA:
These תנאים hold
phrases.notes: He means the תנא קמא and רבי אליעזר of our משנה.

phrases.english: like רבי אליעזר son of רבי יוסי,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
phrases.english: as it was taught: רבי אליעזר son of רבי יוסי said:
I heard that the owners can make a קרבן פיגול.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי אִית לְהוּ דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא's explanation of the משנה from steps 10–11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's תנאים agree that an owner's thought can ruin the שחיטה, like רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי.

steps.title: The argument is about a נכרי who said nothing
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא says a נכרי's thought ruins the שחיטה only if we heard him say it. רבי אליעזר says we assume a נכרי has עבודה זרה in mind even if he said nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the תנא קמא holds: if we heard him say he means it for עבודה זרה, yes, it is ruined. If not, it is not ruined, because we do not assume that a נכרי's unspoken thought is for עבודה זרה. רבי אליעזר holds: even if we did not hear him say it, we assume a נכרי's unspoken thought is for עבודה זרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the exact point the תנא קמא and רבי אליעזר argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that a נכרי owner's stated thought of עבודה זרה ruins the שחיטה. They argue only about a נכרי who said nothing. The תנא קמא does not assume anything about him, while רבי אליעזר assumes the worst.

keyTerms.meaning: a נכרי's unspoken thought is for idol worship
we heard him say what he intends
the first, unnamed opinion in the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree here that a stated thought of עבודה זרה ruins the שחיטה. The only question is what to assume when the נכרי said nothing.

phrases.english: But the first tanna holds:
if we heard him say that he intends it (for idol worship), yes, it is ruined;
if not, it is not ruined,
because the claim that the unspoken thought of a gentile
is for idol worship, we do not say.
רבי אליעזר holds:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא שַׁמְעִינֵיהּ דְּחַשֵּׁיב,
phrases.english: even though we did not hear him say that he intends it,
that the unspoken thought of a gentile
is for idol worship, we do say.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the shared basis from step 12 and pinpoints the dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: an unspoken thought is not assumed to be for עבודה זרה. רבי אליעזר: it is assumed to be for עבודה זרה.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: an owner's thought never counts
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says that even if we heard the נכרי say it, we do not let one person's thought ruin another person's action.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי comes to say: even if we heard him say he means it for עבודה זרה, we do not say that one person's thought counts while another person does the act.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what רבי יוסי adds to the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both the תנא קמא and רבי אליעזר hold that an owner's thought matters. רבי יוסי rejects that idea completely. For him only the שוחט's own thought counts, so the שחיטה is valid even when the נכרי says what he intends.

keyTerms.meaning: one person thinks while another person does the act
we do not say; this rule does not apply

steps.whatToRemember: First version: the תנא קמא and רבי אליעזר argue only about a נכרי who said nothing. רבי יוסי says an owner's thought never ruins someone else's שחיטה.

phrases.english: And רבי יוסי comes to say:
even though we heard him say that he intends it,
that when this one thinks and that one does the act, (the thought counts)
we do not say.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the first explanation by placing רבי יוסי's view from step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי: the owner's thought never ruins a שחיטה done by someone else.

steps.title: Second version: they argue even when the נכרי said it
steps.stepSummary: Others explain that the תנאים argue even when the נכרי said what he intends. The תנא קמא holds that the owner's thought counts only inside the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are those who say: they argue about a case where we heard him say what he intends. The תנא קמא holds: when we say 'one thinks and another does the act,' that applies only inside the מקדש. But outside, it does not apply, because outside from inside (we do not learn).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different way to understand the argument in the משנה. The sentence continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the argument is no longer about a נכרי who said nothing. The תנא קמא agrees that an owner's thought ruins a קרבן inside the מקדש. He holds that this rule does not carry over to חולין slaughtered outside.

keyTerms.meaning: this applies only to
inside the מקדש, meaning קדשים
outside the מקדש, meaning חולין

phrases.english: There are those who say:
they disagree about a case where we heard him say that he intends it,
the first tanna holds:
when we say "this one thinks and that one does the act" (and the thought counts),
that applies only inside,
phrases.notes: Inside means קרבנות in the מקדש.

phrases.english: but outside, it does not apply,
because outside from inside
phrases.notes: The sentence finishes on the next עמוד: we don't learn the rules for outside from the rules for inside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different explanation of the same dispute explained in steps 13–14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Second version, תנא קמא: an owner's thought counts only for קדשים inside the מקדש, not for חולין outside.
